sense.text:
“So they shall make their own tongue to fall upon themselves”. Esau is so prideful that he will tell you he is lying and keep right on doing it, with no repentance and no remorse. The Catholic Church says it with its own mouth: there is no law in the Bible binding anyone to keep Sunday holy; it is a law of the Catholic Church alone, which says that by its own power it abolished the Sabbath day and commanded the first day of the week to be kept holy, and the whole so-called civilized world bows down to it.

That is the history behind it. Sunday means the day of the sun and is of heathen origin. Constantine, the first Roman emperor to take up Christianity, remained a committed sun worshipper and declared Sunday, the day of the sun, the day of rest. A later law forbade believers to worship on the Sabbath, and many were burned to death by the Catholic Church for keeping it. The Council of Laodicea, a bunch of black negroes sitting around making up traditions and what they wanted the Bible to say, just like the think tanks of today, forbade resting on the Sabbath as Judaizing, commanded labour on Saturday, and declared anathema, cursed and cut off, anyone who kept resting on the seventh day. That is why the stores are open on Saturday and you have to send in a letter to get Saturdays off. That is why people say the Sabbath is Jewish stuff, or that it is spiritual, that they rest in Jesus and every day is the Sabbath. And that is why family members who read the truth with their own eyes are afraid to leave the church: they fear being cursed and cut off.

So their own tongue falls upon them. They tell you the lie they put in place to destroy and go against God, and they keep on doing it. That is how much pride they have, and it starts with what we see about the Sabbath day.

“Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth”. Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the things he wants us to know in truth. It is not there to get rich off of with prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we will do and what we will not do. These are the excellent things from the Lord himself.

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The excellent things of Proverbs 22 were written for our learning: for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes.

It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us. We have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Learn and apply: it starts with a change in the mind.

sense.text: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” Actions are weighed with the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things, to learn them and apply them: he wants action behind those things, not lip service, from all of us that he called.

“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself”. He hides himself: he is not dealing with everybody. You do not just call out to him and have him turn around; he answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

“O God of Israel, the Saviour.” So if God has revealed to you that you are an Israelite, if you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means he counted you worthy to reveal his words to you, and you have a chance to know what these excellent things are. You cannot take that lightly, as far too many in this world do who use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their own terms. God does not get down like that. If he is letting you know what his words mean, you had better take heed to him.

“Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think”. This is where pride comes in: letting it overtake us so that we think we are more than we are. If God is revealing himself to you, when he does not deal with everybody, then you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. Even when he gives you the understanding that we are the Israelites and have to keep God’s commandments, you had better not think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

“But to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.”

“That they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still just beasts in his eyes, and that is why we have to humble ourselves and not think too highly of ourselves.

“As the one dieth, so dieth the other”. Man, the beasts, the lions, and the bug that has no real value except to serve the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. Who are you to think so highly of yourself that you can reject what God has written to us in the excellent things and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form and we perish just like everything else. That is where the humbleness comes in.

“Yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast. We come here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you leave and go back to your maker.

precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” The Israelites are gods upon this earth. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” Gods and children of the Most High, and still we die just like men and fall like the princes.

So, just as the animals die, in the grand scheme of things we have no more power than they do. Are we higher up the ladder of God’s creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

sense.text:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what David says we have. “And if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: eighty, if God is merciful. That is how you know the Bible is a true book: get to around forty and you find out David was right. That is why Captain Gideon taught the class about working out, not drinking sodas that calcify the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so that God may be merciful and say, you did real good with that temple I gave you; I will give you eighty years.

“Yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away is the spirit going back to its creator, right back to where it came from. That is the one day all of us are going to fly: when we get up out of this body.

“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what God says. We just read David saying seventy, maybe eighty years: that is the covenant, thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have children. You watch them grow up and you realize you are getting old, and that the covenant God has pronounced upon all, death, is about to come to you too.
“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord.

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death”. That is the reason the covenant has passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came as well. We break it down for those new to the faith, to put the puzzle pieces together of why we die.

“But the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh: you cannot receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh, because flesh and blood cannot enter the kingdom of heaven. And the one thing we had better make sure we do not have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure.

sense.text:
“That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” David says seventy or eighty years; God says a day to him is a thousand years. Do the math in worldly terms: if a thousand years is one day, eighty years is 0.08 of a day, about one hour and fifty-five minutes. An entire human lifetime is less than two hours in the eyes of God, and it could be even less than that, depending on his mercy. Broken down further, a whole day of ours is like a quarter of a second to him.

That is why the Bible calls him the Ancient of days: he has no beginning and no end, and the concept of time does not apply to the Most High God. No wonder he does not worry about time and does not stir the cup until he is ready, while we stress over three to five business days and get mad when the shipping takes more than two. You live eighty years, come back to him, and to him you just left.

precepts.why:
“My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee”. This is why the scriptures say things like this. We are here a while and it feels like forever: it takes forever to become an adult, waiting on a driver’s license, waiting to turn twenty-one, to be thirty-six and forty. We are going through it right now and it seems like forever; Lord, come save us; they are doing their worst.

“But shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” Shortly: in a few minutes of God’s time your life is going to be over, and in an hour or so you are going to see the destruction of your enemy, and then have a lifetime of God time. Eternal.

“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” That is why God says a small moment: it is not even two hours to him, not even a day.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment”. It is just a moment; that is what God says. Start thinking about it like that: I am only here for a short while.

sense.text: “Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.” Because God set up the elders: he is the one that set them up, for the younger to learn his ways from them and for them to feed you with his wisdom and knowledge. So God tells the younger to humble themselves to the elders, to the leaders. “Yea, all of you be subject one to another”: all of you have respect one for another, but there is a hierarchy in God’s eyes. “And be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.”

“Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God”. Through this whole Bible God talks about humbling and being meek like Moses. We are here only a moment, not even two hours in the eyes of God, so you had better humble yourself.

“That he may exalt you in due time”. When is that? When you go back to him. That is the real exaltation we want: a crown from God Almighty. You cannot get any higher than the Almighty God putting a crown on your head.
“Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He knows you only have a short amount of time to be here, so your care should be cast on him.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Here you have to use your spiritual eyes. Why would Peter put the devil seeking whom he may devour right after all the humbling and the humility? Because Satan is out there looking for the prideful, those who think they know more than God in the short time they have been here. Satan has been here just as long and does not deal with time either; the only time he worries about is when Christ comes back and his clock starts.

Satan will use you when you walk in pride to destroy you and everybody and everything around you, because pride does not affect just one person. Being proud of your heritage and of who God made you is one thing; there is humility in that. Being prideful is having an excessively high opinion of oneself, an inflated sense of self-importance: arrogance and superiority; disdain that looks down on those deemed unworthy; an inability to admit fault or ask for help; competing, rejoicing in others’ failures and disliking their successes; an inflated ego that needs to prove itself. How can you look down on anyone when your life is but a vapour, an hour and some change in God’s eyes, and you are a beast going into the dirt just like they are? It happens to the best of us, which is why we have to examine ourselves as Israelites first, so we do not become the pride of our own heart.

precepts.why:
“And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. In the shortness of time, this is what God calls what we are going through. We feel it and we are going through it, complaining, crying, fasting, doing what we can to make it through. We are not even at the point of being persecuted and put to death, and he calls this a little chastising.

“For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” So we have to endure to the end, and he will exalt us in due time.

sense.text: “Pride was not made for men”. Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the competitive, self-centred, inflated ego: God says it was not made for you. You are nothing but the dust that shall return to where it came from. “Nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Anger gets you nowhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

“The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is why you have to watch out for pride as you get older: you start thinking you can make your own decisions about whether to serve God, whether to obey your Father. Pride is when you begin to depart from the commandments God gave us.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”. When you turn away from your maker you automatically walk in sin. None of those who do not keep the commandments of God has a good heart, though we grew up in the world thinking that if we did not steal, rob or kill anybody, we were good. You can lie to yourself, but it is still a lie, and God knows it, and so do you when you sleep at night. You know it when somebody starts pulling out scriptures and you are not trying to hear it: that is how you know your life is a lie.

“Pride is hateful before God and man: and by both doth one commit iniquity.” Pride is the beginning of going into sin, and it is hateful before God. Those in Christianity who say we do not have to keep those laws are not on the right side of God: they have departed from their God and maker and his ways, and they are in sin. Do not deceive yourself.

You can repent, hopscotch right back over to the right side of God and stay there. But if you disobey him with pride, you are on the side of God’s hatred, and everything God does not like comes to an expiration date. He gets rid of it; he removes it with judgment.

precepts.why: “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. That is why you cannot walk in pride, and why it was not made for you. You did not put one finger on your hand. You did not put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the creator of it from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image. He did not consult you about where the knee should go, how high up the leg, what the arch of the foot should look like, what skin tone to give you or what your hair should be like. None of us was included in that conversation. We did not make ourselves.

“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”. You do not know how the spirit was even made, and the body does not function without a spirit in it. It might be jacked up, crooked like the Esau that is in them, but no body is walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made it.

“Nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best it can, but they do not know what God did to make that. God gives man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God, putting a rod on a woman and cutting a man’s off. That is why the Bible says beware of science when it opposes God. “Even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.”

“Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.” The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to its maker. All of it belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to. Young kids and teenagers do not really fight with this; it is as we get older that we start smelling ourselves and saying, this is what I want to do, forgetting that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God.

The way parents look at a grown man of forty-seven with gray hair and still say, you will always be my baby: apply that to your life with God. The Lord controls it all; he is the God of all spirits. You do not get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. You have to keep his commandments, because he is still your Father, and that is what he said to do.

sense.text: “These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him”.

“A proud look” is the first one on the list. God hates it. Walk in pride, depart from your maker as if you know better than your Daddy, and you are immediately on the wrong side: it is the first thing on his list. You are nothing but dirt on this earth; you are a beast; you are going to die. You have no power over your life. God says, the only reason this negro blinks is because of me, and he is going to sit here and tell me all this gluteus maximus on these black women out here is for him to look at? Negro, I made your eyes, and I told you not to look at a woman like that. I made your nose, your legs, your body parts and the mind you think with. Who do you think you are? Humble yourself.

It is especially those who know the scriptures and will not do anything with them: they know what the scriptures say and choose not to obey the commandments. That is a proud look, and they are in bad shape. Arrogance and superiority, disdain, inability to admit fault, competitive and self-centred, an inflated ego: God says those who think like this and move like that are first on his list. Then “a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood”.

“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Whenever you see somebody fall off, going from here to there, there is some form of pride in that man or that woman that they do not want to address: an inflated ego, disdain, haughty looks, not coming back to God. You might not have seen it; they might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

It is a warning. When you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, moving a little too arrogant, pride comes before the fall. So say, oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing.

It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, which all happened because of pride. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he wanted to do his own thing, mocking the leadership above him and going with his buddies. We are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The Lord’s mighty and strong one “shall cast down to the earth with the hand.” “The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet”: destroyed. Pride destroyed the northern kingdom.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall because of pride, but the southern kingdom is not exempt from that pride either. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah was prideful too: they looked at what their brother was doing, and God said they followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem is Benjamin and Levi: all of the southern kingdom was in pride in God’s eyes.

“This evil people”: pride makes an evil people, “which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart”. When pride comes, they separate from God, as Ecclesiasticus 10 says: you separate yourself from your maker, “and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them”. They “shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When you are full of pride you are no good in God’s eyes.

That is the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You had better listen up. Be not proud, O Israel; do not separate yourself from him. It comes from God, so humble yourself and do as he tells you, because he is our creator and controls all of this. It could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I am done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do; and Christ would crack the sky. But not on the surface, saying forgive me while you wait to get out of here and do what you want. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us who are repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom.

And pride is not always boisterous or blatant. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified or owed, saying I am good or I am fine when you know you are not, shutting down, thinking you do not need anybody, always pointing the finger at somebody else and not yourself. Subtle pride destroys you where you are, just as it destroyed us in the kingdom, and Satan still has you.

“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” This is where you have to examine yourself. Are you ignorant of Satan’s devices? Has he been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It might be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself. Satan has many devices; he is able to transform himself into an angel of light, and he knows how to get to you to hold you back. Is Satan’s device getting you?

Even the fat brothers: too prideful to change their eating habits.

“The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God.”

“For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and had a brother killed, putting out a hit on him. So what does it mean that he did not put away God’s statutes? When the prophet Nathan brought it to him, he said, that is me. God was going to take the child; he fasted and prayed, and if God let the child live, so be it, and if he took him, he would not be mad. When it happened he washed his face, ate some bread and said it was the Lord’s judgment. He was not prideful, saying, I am the king, I can have as many women as I want. He acknowledged God’s judgments and humbled himself.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point that God said David is a man after his own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. He did not rise up in pride and say, I can do what I want, I am king of Israel, God chose me. He acknowledged his sins.
“A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Look what pride does: it brings a man low. And pride has destroyed every kingdom on the earth, as the kings show.
Pride destroyed the king of Assyria. “In the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah”, Sennacherib “came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them.”

Then come big words from his herald and messenger, Rabshakeh: “Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?” “Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?”

Eliakim, Shebna and Joah ask him to speak “in the Syrian language”, so that everybody on the wall will not find out what he is saying. He answers that he was sent to “the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you”, then cries “with a loud voice in the Jews’ language”, “Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.” Big words. These are the words of the king of Assyria.

“Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?” “Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?” All that pride came out of the king of Assyria’s mouth by way of his messenger.
God heard all that smack and all that tough talk. “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria”.

Listen to the aggression in these words: “The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn”. She is up there laughing at his tough talk: who does this dude think he is? “The daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee”, like, I am about to whoop his ass: like a parent who told you not to do it, laughing because he is about to tear you up. You are not going to one-up God; God is going to one-up you. That goes for all those making videos mocking God’s prophets.

“For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand”: 185,000 destroyed by one of God’s angels. When the sun went down they were all alive; at the crack of the morning, “behold, they were all dead”. For talking prideful against God, everybody had to die.

He killed all the soldiers, but God said, no, no, I am hunting his ass: I am hunting Sennacherib. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” He thought he got away. Then, “as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god”, “Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword”: God let his own sons kill him for all that prideful talk, “and they escaped into the land of Armenia”, and his other son reigned in his stead, glad they killed him. Pride destroyed the king of Assyria.
Babylon is the head of gold in Daniel’s dream. “Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold”, and “he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.”

In his pride he set up an image of himself and said everybody should worship it: “ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up”, “And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.” Nebuchadnezzar got prideful too.

America does the same thing now with the flag. You do not bow down to it; you have to stand up, salute it and honour it. It is the same as ancient Babylon, just a different way.

God sent Nebuchadnezzar a dream, and this is “the decree of the most High”: “they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field, and they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen”, “till thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.” As Proverbs says, pride will bring a man low: God would make him walk on all fours and eat grass with the dew of heaven on his back.

“All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar. At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon.” Look what he said to himself: “Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?” What does God call America? Babylon the great. Nebuchadnezzar called Babylon great himself.

“While the word was in the king’s mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee.” That kingdom is gone, taken: pride, trying to make people worship you. He forgot what Daniel had told him a year before. “Until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”: until you humble yourself, your ass is going to eat grass. Damn. And he did humble himself: he came back and said there is no God like the God of Daniel.

Cyrus the Persian humbled himself: he let all Israel go back to where they came from, paid for everything, let nobody touch them, and told Ezra to let him know if he needed anything, so God let him rule. But for the others that had pride, here come the Greeks. “About that time came Antiochus with dishonour out of the country of Persia”.

“The judgment of God now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” He had the same thought the king of Assyria did, talking proudly against God’s kingdom.

The Lord Almighty “smote him with an incurable and invisible plague”, a plague inside his body you could not see: “as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”. As soon as he spoke those proud words, straight diarrhoea, instantly. “And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange” torments. You know how those Greeks got down, and the writer is saying it: God said, I have something for you, payback as soon as you speak proudly.

This is the pride of Esau: torn up, inflammation all in his stomach, and still talking. He “still was filled with pride, breathing out fire” against the Jews. That is how much hatred they have for us, bred in them: a perpetual hatred, as Ezekiel says. They go into their grave hating us. Then “he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained.”

“And when he himself could not abide his own smell, he said these words, It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself” as if he were God. Check yourself before you wreck yourself. All these kingdoms continually fall because of pride, and it is no different with what is coming here.

Now we are down to the Romans, which is what Herod was. “Upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.” Black folk always think a white man is God. God always has to remind you who he is.

“And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America, it does not matter. God destroying them is the judgment for it.

“Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth.” All those kings that ruled are judges of the earth at their appointed times, ruling all nations in their times: “Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.” “For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels.” All that power and rulership is given to them by God, and the same with us: it was given to us by God.

“Because, being ministers of his kingdom, ye have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of God; Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places. For mercy will soon pardon the meanest”, that is, the lowest, “but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.”

You shall be tormented when you are a king in pride, when you rule in pride, because your counsels, the things you do and your rulership will be judged by God. If it is not according to his ways, he brings you down. That is for every single king he has set up, including all of us, the kings of the earth of Israel.

“Unto you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that ye may learn wisdom, and not fall away. For they that keep holiness holily shall be judged holy: and they that have learned such things shall find what to answer.” “Wherefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and ye shall be instructed.”

“Therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom.” You cannot rule a kingdom without wisdom, and you have to have humility to gain God’s wisdom. “If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres”, if we want to be kings as we were created to be, “O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” If you walk in pride, you are done for. The only way our kingdom will last forever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that the kingdom comes down immediately, as it did with all the nations before us, and today.

“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”. All those kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God and they serve idol gods. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God: they do not, and they fall. It is no different with Babylon the great.

“Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Edom is the white man, the Caucasian; that is his biblical name. For those who do not believe it, show us somebody else that is like this. This Edomite has the most gods: the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one here, in different forms.
“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.”

Greatly despised for their pride. Out of all the kings we read about, the Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks and Romans, none is more prideful than this Edomite here in Babylon the great. None is more prideful than Esau. “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”, and he is so prideful he says “in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They have more pride than anybody that ever walked the face of the earth. One of their government came on the news and said, we own the moon, why not Greenland? That is pride.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”. They are so prideful that they went to the moon and claimed it for their own, something they did not even create. They will even steal the moon, and they will not let other nations plant a flag there and say, we conquered this. They went there and said, the eagle has landed. That is how prideful they are.

There is a reason behind Edom’s pride. “The devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me”. “If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible. So when you see In God We Trust on the money, he is not talking about anybody in this Bible.

Here is the proof. “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”. “For the wicked boasteth of his heart’s desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the Lord abhorreth. The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” In God We Trust on that money has nothing to do with the God of the Bible; God is not in any of his thoughts.

Look at the way they treat the peaceable ones, the lowly, those who cannot defend themselves: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, with no army, no guns, no military training. How they treat the minorities is how you judge whether somebody is prideful or humble in the eyes of God. God had laws in the Bible to look out for the poor: do not take all the grapes off your vine; leave some for the poor, your people. Does Esau do that? Hell no. He will take your damn nationality, take your race, and then call himself that. He is not humble at all.

“His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.” We see all of that going on right now. “He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved”. “His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud”. He murders the innocent: “his eyes are privily set against the poor.” Black wealth is like ten cents compared to a hundred dollars of white folks.

“He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor”. That is the movie The Burial with Jamie Foxx. Esau used his power of insurance and made a contract with the national black church, so that all the caskets in the inner cities came from him, and the churches were made sales reps to poor black people. They overbought the package, and when they died there still was not enough money to bury the very people who had paid for it: overpriced coffins, so you are in debt when you are dead. Asked whether he felt a certain type of way about robbing the poor for decades, the man said, absolutely not. Evil.

It is the same with the white man who says black people are not owed reparations because it was their ancestors, not them, who went through it, while he still lives off the slave money and the businesses his ancestors made from slavery, whipping backs, killing and hanging people with fear. Trump has the money to give every Greenland citizen a hundred thousand dollars, but nothing for the descendants of those who built this nation, though America prints its own money. When it comes to the poor, no remorse. They say it was not them, but you have to pay for it. That is your reparations.

“Concerning Edom, thus saith the Lord of hosts”: God concerning the white man, to make it plain. “Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?” In easy terms: have you lost your mind?

“But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself”. He cannot hide. The prophets of God are back on the earth and the spirit of the Lord is here, telling you who Esau is, showing you the one who lives and thinks in the pride of his heart, as if he is above everything and above reproach.

“Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken”. For the pride we had among us as a nation, we have been destroyed; look at us and you can see we have drunk the cup of God. “And art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.”

“For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men. Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart”. The power they have, the laws they have made, the way they have rigged the system against everybody on earth: the pride of Esau has deceived them. “Though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.”

That is the moon landing, 1969. The moment they set foot there in the pride of their heart and said the eagle has landed, they started going down. As was taught in the Sabbath classes a year or two ago, when they landed on the moon is when the Israelites started hitting the streets. God brings them down with the word of God: the Israelites rising up and gathering themselves together. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down, and his kingdom is being destroyed right in front of our eyes. They thought these negroes and Hispanics who could not read and were running for their lives would never rise up, and that reading the Bible would never be the destruction of their kingdom. O prideful one, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

“Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof. As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the Lord, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.” God is going to wipe this place off the face of the earth with fire, just as he did Sodom and Gomorrah for their pride as well, because that is what was found in Sodom and Gomorrah: pride, going after strange flesh.

We are glad Trump is in office: he is showing the true colours and the nature of Esau, Edom. Asked whether anything could check his power on the world stage, he said only one thing, his own morality, his own mind. That sounds just like Antiochus, full of wrath, speaking proudly. God heard him.

“Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud”. Nobody is prouder than Esau. “For thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee.” They think God forgot their original sin, as they like to call slavery. God has not forgotten, because we are still here, and they have not let up the continual stroke: still misusing and abusing God’s children, hunting down the Latinos in the street, who are part of the twelve tribes of Israel. He is going to visit you.

“And the most proud shall stumble and fall”. God has not taken him out yet, because he has prophecies to push forward, but he touched him to let him know he heard those proud words: chronic venous insufficiency, leg veins that do not let the blood flow back up to the heart. Now we see Trump has bad feet: the proud is going to stumble. This kingdom is going to fall, “and none shall raise him up”. Once God is done with this place, it is over.

“And I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.” Just as in ancient Sodom and Gomorrah, he is going to burn this: Canada, Mexico, everything on this side of the earth, the neighbouring cities, gone. God does not want any of it any more.

Asked whether God is proud of him, Trump said he thinks God is very proud of the job he has done. The Bible is a true book: “I am against thee, O thou most proud”.
“And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood”: that lion is Christ. “And I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”: to America.

“Hear thou, I will talk with thee, and the Highest shall say unto thee, Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” The end is going to come through Esau.

“And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world”, “and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression”. Blacks and Hispanics know about that oppression, and our brothers from other countries coming here are finding out about it now. He rules with much wicked oppression, all the way from Iran to America, “and so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit.”

“For the earth hast thou not judged with truth.” There is no truth here. “For thou hast afflicted the meek”: that is us. “Thou hast hurt the peaceable”, “thou hast loved liars”: you love lies. “And destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm.” The blacks and the Hispanics getting chased down by ICE have done nobody any harm. They are trying to get the low-level job to earn a little more than they could in South America, Mexico and Central America, minding their own business, while Trump calls them all rapists and murderers.

“Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty.” God has remembered. As much as they want to think God is proud of them and present themselves as a Christian country, their pride has come up to him. “The Highest also hath looked upon the proud”: the pride of thine heart. “And, behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled.” This place will be destroyed, thus saith the Lord.
